question.text: A commodity producer who will sell output in the future should adopt:

answer.text: A short hedge — sell futures to lock in the selling price
A long hedge — buy futures contracts
Buy call options to protect against price decline
Wait until harvest to decide on hedging

explanation.text: The Logic: Producers/farmers lock in their selling price using a short hedge (selling futures). If prices fall, the futures gain offsets the lower spot revenue. The source defines a short hedge as the sale of futures and gives a producer short-hedge example. The Trap: Long hedge is for buyers (processors), not sellers. Call options protect against rising prices. Waiting removes the protective benefit of hedging. Note: Farmers may lock the selling price of the upcoming harvest during sowing season using a short hedge.
